top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Granfondo Top Dolomites' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
132ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
9,121ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Road-specific control matters at Granfondo Top Dolomites. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 69 miles.
At Granfondo Top Dolomites, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
9,121ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Granfondo Top Dolomites. Train it until it feels boring.
69 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Low-cadence force work supports 9,121ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Granfondo Top Dolomites. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Base fitness for Granfondo Top Dolomites. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
